title: Entangling General History Mechanisms with Domain-Specific Undo Actions
pattern: A general-purpose history/undo mechanism is coupled to specific domain actions by branching on a concrete domain enumeration or struct type inside the history manager.
why_bad: Creates a circular dependency and information leakage. Adding a new undoable action to the application requires modifying the general-purpose `History` manager, preventing it from being isolated as a reusable, general-purpose component.
detection: A generic-looking manager class (like `History` or `UndoManager`) performs pattern matching, casting, or conditional dispatch on domain-specific enums or classes.
counterexample: Simple, highly localized undo lists nested entirely within a single component. Marked `Context-dependent` if no external reuse is intended.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 9, "Example: editor undo mechanism", p. 451-454.
